name: Chogha Golan domesticated-type emmer
description: At Chogha Golan, residents had access to emmer wheat with domestication-type traits in an early agricultural setting.

impact.note: One site's remains showing access to domestic-type emmer in early farming; farming is a new ability, but this site's own legacy is unclear.

date.label: Approximately 9800 cal BP (7850 BCE)
date.basis: Approximate archaeological context; calibrated BP values use 1950 as reference.

events.statement: At Chogha Golan, residents had access to emmer wheat with domestication-type traits in an early agricultural setting.

evidence.supports: The abstract reports domesticated-type emmer around 9800 cal BP in a long local archaeobotanical sequence.

evidence.locator: Chogha Golan, Sampling and laboratory methods, and Conclusion
evidence.supports: Study of the local sequence records a decline in the relative representation of wild grasses when domesticated emmer becomes prominent around 9,800 cal BP. The authors consider the evidence insufficient to determine whether the earlier wild cereals were cultivated.

events.caveats: The domestication traits were recovered at Chogha Golan. Where they developed and whether the earlier wild cereals were cultivated locally remain unsettled.

earliest_record.rationale: Around 9800 cal BP dates the site’s documented occurrence of domestication-type emmer.

caveats: The domestication traits were recovered at Chogha Golan. Where they developed and whether the earlier wild cereals were cultivated locally remain unsettled.

research.note: The added study provides a fuller reading of the local sequence while drawing on the same excavations as the shorter 2013 report.
